topic: Mistral raises EUR 3B for open-weight frontier AI
title: Mistral tonight: Small 4 runs, Large 3 waits
description: One rule decides which Mistral model runs on your hardware tonight.
hook_candidates: Three billion euros, and the open-weight pledge is already half true. * (A, number-shock)
You can already run Mistral tonight. Just not the six hundred seventy-five billion one. * (B, named-contradiction)
Six hundred seventy-five billion parameters, and it still wants eight GPUs.
Europe's biggest round ever just bet on downloadable weights.
Mistral raised three billion euros. Your GPU cares about one number.
The pledge says open weights. Your gaming PC already has proof.
You run open models at home. Mistral just made that a business model.
One hundred nineteen billion parameters, and it runs tonight.
Samsung just led three billion euros into open weights.
Frontier AI was supposed to leave your desk behind. It didn't.
narration_full: You can already run Mistral tonight. Just not the six hundred seventy-five billion one. You run open models on a gaming PC or Mac. Mistral just raised three billion euros promising open weights, published files you run yourself. Both are Apache two point oh, a license allowing free commercial use. Both are mixtures of experts, an office lighting only the rooms in use, though you own the building. Small four lights six and a half billion parameters per word. Now the totals. Small four, one hundred nineteen billion parameters, runs on your box. The six hundred seventy-five billion one wants eight datacenter GPUs. So the rule: fits your GPU, Small four. Needs a datacenter, Large three.

analogy.vehicle: Giant office building where you only light the rooms in use
analogy.mapping: Small 4 is a 119B-parameter building but only 6.5B lights are on per token, which is why it feels fast despite its size.
analogy.limit: You still have to buy the whole building: disk and VRAM must hold all the experts even though only a few fire at a time.

scenes.narration: You can already run Mistral tonight. Just not the six hundred seventy-five billion one.
scenes.visual_brief: Frame 1: two model name cards side by side; on 'run Mistral tonight' the Small 4 card scales in bright from 0.30 s; on 'six hundred seventy-five billion' the Large 3 card fades in greyed out.

scenes.narration: You run open models on a gaming PC or Mac. Mistral just raised three billion euros promising open weights, published files you run yourself.
scenes.visual_brief: On 'gaming PC or Mac' a desktop tower and laptop fade in; on 'three billion euros' the €3B figure rises in place above them; on 'published files' a download arrow lands on the machines.

scenes.narration: Both are Apache two point oh, a license allowing free commercial use.
scenes.visual_brief: Both model cards return; on 'Apache two point oh' a license tag scales in, bridging the two cards to show one shared license.

scenes.narration: Both are mixtures of experts, an office lighting only the rooms in use, though you own the building. Small four lights six and a half billion parameters per word.
scenes.on_screen_text: MoE: lit rooms, owned building | Small 4: 6.5B per word
scenes.visual_brief: On 'office lighting only the rooms in use' a floor-plan grid fades in with a few rooms lit; on 'six and a half billion' the Small 4 label rises with 6.5B beside a mostly-dark Large 3 floor.

scenes.narration: Now the totals. Small four, one hundred nineteen billion parameters, runs on your box. The six hundred seventy-five billion one wants eight datacenter GPUs.
scenes.visual_brief: On 'one hundred nineteen billion' the Small 4 card settles onto the desktop tower and fits; on 'eight datacenter GPUs' a server rack fades in beside Large 3, which stays off the desk.

scenes.narration: So the rule: fits your GPU, Small four. Needs a datacenter, Large three.
scenes.visual_brief: On 'fits your GPU' the Small 4 card settles onto the desktop; the two-card frame rhymes with frame 1; final half second wordmark settle, no further motion.

notes_for_review: A: Fortune benchmark claim softened to 'eighteen months behind' with the 'some benchmarks' qualifier kept; 'fits your gaming GPU' was replaced with 'downloadable tonight' because the brief carries no fit claim for Ministral. B: 'forty-one billion active' was cut to stay inside the five-number cap; the screen keeps the verbatim node line.
